name: What if the project scope changes after permits are submitted?

mainEntity.name: What happens if the scope changes after commercial permits are already submitted?
mainEntity.text: What happens if the scope changes after commercial permits are already submitted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Scope changes after permit submission can create a chain reaction. Even a small adjustment may require revised drawings, updated engineering, resubmittal, and another round of review. If the change affects life safety, structural items, accessibility, or occupancy, the impact can be larger. That is why commercial project managers try to lock major decisions before permits are filed. If a change is unavoidable, it should be documented, priced, approved, and incorporated into the schedule as soon as possible. Owners should expect potential delays and added fees if revisions are substantial. The best way to minimize disruption is to keep design coordination tight before permit submission and to avoid late-stage changes unless they truly improve the project outcome.
acceptedAnswer.description: If scope changes after permits are submitted, the plans may need revisions, resubmittal, or additional review before construction can proceed. Depending on the change, the schedule and budget may both increase, so the change should be documented and approved immediately.
